Paged Attention Decode on H100 — official score 0.3606

Paged Attention Decode on H100 — official score 0.3606
Memory summary

The final kernel uses two Triton stages: stage one processes 32-token sequence partitions and writes partial softmax statistics and weighted values; stage two combines those partials into the output. The official H100 result passed correctness and scored 0.3606 peak_fraction, the geometric mean of achieved bandwidth divided by the 2039 GB/s reference peak.

Relevant prior context

The stage-one grid assigns work by sequence partition, KV head, and batch element. It maps each token through the block table, shares each KV head’s work across its grouped query heads, and loads K and V from the packed [K | V] cache. Each partition computes a local maximum, exponential sum, and weighted V accumulator.

Triton initially failed compilation because the probability tensor and V had different dtypes. Casting probabilities to bf16 fixed the dot operand mismatch, and the correctness checker passed. A 64-token partition variant benchmarked at 0.3885 peak_fraction in the trace. A 128-token variant passed correctness but its benchmark was stopped before timings arrived. The agent reverted to 64, tried 32, confirmed correctness, and left block_n = 32 in the final solution. The final official run’s score is 0.3606; the earlier 0.3885 is not its result.

The final reduction combines partition statistics with a global maximum:

m_final = tl.max(m, axis=0)
alpha = tl.exp(m - m_final)
denom = tl.sum(alpha * l, axis=0)
numer = tl.sum(acc * alpha[:, None], axis=0)
result = numer / denom
Important non-obvious context

This is a memory-regime score: each shape’s achieved GB/s is divided by the stated 2039 GB/s peak, then the shape fractions are combined by geometric mean. The task tested five shapes, bf16 data, and 30 performance trials. The environment trace identified NVIDIA H100 PCIe (9, 0), CUDA 13.0, and Triton 3.6.0.

The official leaderboard calculation places this run at rank 9 of 18 cells, with 17 scored cells and a board-leading score of 0.5521. The catalog marks the run unaudited; the manifest also says unaudited and rejected: false. The rundetail reports correctness as true and annotation_verdict: null, so there is no separate audit verdict in these files.
